summary: Target state of the community server as data. Nothing here is applied to a server; the path that applies it is decided in docs/adr/0010-bot-rights-and-apply-path.md and not built.

metrics.measures: How many members hold one role.
metrics.source: The platform's count of members per role. No message is read and no member id is kept.

metrics.measures: How many days have passed since the last message in one channel.
metrics.source: The time carried by the id of the channel's last message. No message is read and no member id is kept.

roles.name: @everyone
roles.purpose: Every member. The base of all permissions.

roles.name: Operator
roles.purpose: Runs the server and is the last instance for every decision.

roles.name: Moderator

roles.name: Contributor

opening.subject: interest-home-lab
opening.reasoning: A room needs enough people that a message gets an answer the same day. Twelve interested members, on every daily reading for two weeks, is a first guess; it is replaced once the lounge shows how many interested members a daily conversation takes.

closing.subject: home-lab
closing.reasoning: A room whose last message is a month old makes the server look deserted. Thirty days is a first guess.

automation.what: Answers the ask command from the documentation, visible only to the member who asked.
Reads the first message of a new post in the support forum and replies first with excerpts, only when the member set the opt-in tag at its creation (ADR-0020).
Shows new discussions of the listed repositories on the server with a link back.
Carries out what a moderator does through it, deleting a message or timing a member out, and writes the trail of those actions.
Gives and takes the interest, language and notification roles from the member's own choice, made through the areas command.
Opens and closes the threshold areas and language rooms from the readings of their rules. Until it is built, the operator does this by hand.
Posts own releases and security advisories as they happen, and everything else as one digest per channel per day.
Gives and takes the supporter roles from the funding platforms.
Gives the Contributor role to a member whose contribution was merged. Needs a link between a member and a forge account, which is its own record.
Filters spam and obvious abuse before a person sees it, and writes each flagged case into the moderators' queue channel.
Invites people and grants the moderator and subject guide roles. The bot grants neither.
Reads and answers the private threads in the ticket channel.
Schedules events and opens the voice room for their duration.

Applies this definition to the server on one path: plan, dry run, apply, read-only compare. Every run uses the bot's identity: for the first set-up the operator raises the bot's role for the run and lowers it afterwards; with its three rights the bot runs the same path for its own changes. Not built.
Compares the platform's filter rules and the server's verification level with the definition and applies a difference through plan and apply.

Holds a new member back from every action on the server until they completed the server's screening form (Discord's Membership Screening). It is switched on by hand in the server's settings. Observed on 2026-10-11 as the server feature MEMBER_VERIFICATION_GATE_ENABLED; what the form asks was not read.

verification.reasoning: Chosen, not measured. A new account has to be older than five minutes before it can write, which stops an account made for one spam run. The level above it holds every new member back for ten minutes after joining, and Membership Screening already holds them until they completed the form.

filter_rules.name: Spam
filter_rules.purpose: Blocks messages the platform recognises as spam and writes each case into the moderators' queue.
filter_rules.reasoning: Chosen, not measured. The platform's own spam detection, the first case of spam and obvious abuse that ADR-0005 leaves to the platform.

filter_rules.name: Mass mentions
filter_rules.purpose: Blocks a message that mentions many members or roles at once, and a raid of such messages, and writes each case into the moderators' queue.
filter_rules.reasoning: Chosen, not measured. Ten different mentions in one message is more than a question to a few people needs; the limit is corrected once the server has members.

filter_rules.name: Slurs and sexual content
filter_rules.purpose: Blocks messages with words from the platform's lists of slurs and of sexual content and writes each case into the moderators' queue.
filter_rules.reasoning: Chosen, not measured. The two lists cover obvious abuse in the sense of ADR-0005. The list of swearing is left out: swearing alone is not abuse on this server, and a moderator handles a case of it.
